newsitem.title: USA: Verdict reached in Simpson civil case.
newsitem.headline: Verdict reached in Simpson civil case.

text.p: The jury in O.J. Simpson's civil trial reached a verdict on Tuesday, and court officials said it would be read in open court by mid-evening.

A decision was reached in the sixth day of jury deliberations and court spokeswoman Jerrianne Hayslett said it would be announced as soon as the participants in the wrongful-death lawsuit arrived at the courthouse.
Crowds began massing outside the Santa Monica courthouse as the news spread. Hayslett said the court session would probably begin between 8:30 and 9 p.m. EST (0130 and 0200 GMT on Wednesday)

The jury of six men and six women earlier on Tuesday listened to four hours of readings of crucial evidence in the case, including Simpson's testimony of his activities on the night his ex-wife and her friend were stabbed to death.
Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman by a criminal jury in October 1995.
He then battled a wrongful-death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims and could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages if he is found responsible for the murders.

The jury on Tuesday also heard readings of the testimony of limousine driver Allan Park, who said he arrived at Simpson's estate at 10:22 p.m. on the night of the murders, but didn't see the former football star until 10:55 p.m.
The jury was also read portions of Simpson's testimony regarding a violent argument with his then-wife which occured on Jan. 1, 1991, and left Nicole Brown Simpson bruised and battered.
In that reading the jury was reminded that Simpson said he never hit his ex-wife but took "full responsibility" for her injuries.

The panel also heard a reading from the sworn testimony of Simpson's best friend Al Cowlings about how he took Nicole Brown Simpson to the hospital to be treated for her injuries and how she told him that Simpson had beaten her.
